messages:
jamie: alert -> multiple svc owners, seeing large spike in NAT gateway conn resets in us-east-1-edge, symptoms: 502/504 and client conn resets, CloudWatch shows SNAT port utilization ~98% on nat-0a1b2c3d :cry:
jamie: CloudWatch query: metrics(NATGateway, PortUsage) -> sum by (NatGatewayId) 98.2% at 11:07 UTC
jamie: observed error from model-pull sidecars: 
```
error: connect ECONNRESET
while fetching model from s3://redwood-models/large-v2
```

maria: which subnets are hitting the nat? is this single AZ?
alex: looks like main edge fleet in az a is saturated. ss output from a box: `ss -s` -> "TCP: *: 105k established, 92k time_wait"
alex: `ss -tn | grep TIME_WAIT | wc -l` -> 92034
oncall-bot: incident created: INC-2026-9042 paging sre_lead,maria
devin: pushed a sidecar change 20m ago that increases parallel model pulls from 8->24 per pod, rolling to all edge nodes in that AZ
sre_lead: immediate mitigation options: 1) add additional NAT gateway(s) in same AZ or enable cross-AZ egress, 2) roll back sidecar parallelism, 3) reduce cold model pull fanout via queued pulls, 4) deploy an egress proxy to multiplex connections
maria: we can flip a second NAT in subnets quickly — provisioning time ~5m, will that help given ephemeral port exhaustion?
sre_lead: yes, adding NATs increases available 5-tuple SNAT space (effectively more ports per IP) — helps short-term while we reduce parallelism
jamie: spun up nat-0d4e5f6g in az-a, routing table updated for edge-subnet-1 -> verifying
jamie: after NAT add: port usage dropped to 63% on nat-0a1b2c3d and nat-0d4e5f6g showing 15% (combined coverage improved)
alex: long-term fixes: enforce HTTP keepalive/connection pooling in sidecar, avoid per-request short-lived TCP connections to S3/model store, enable AWS S3 VPC endpoints to remove public NAT egress for pulls
devin: reverting parallelism to 8 for now (rolled back to 40% of pods) — telemetry shows error rate falling
maria: quick sysctl we used on a test host to widen ephemeral ports: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="15000 61000"` and `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144` — note: conntrack must be sized accordingly
sre_lead: note: avoid tcp_tw_recycle/tcp_tw_reuse on NATGW setups — can break clients and is not recommended. Also TCP TIME_WAIT counts are expected with many short connections; connection reuse is the right fix
jamie: creating action items in doc: 1) prod rollback for sidecar parallel pulls (dev) 2) ensure S3 VPC endpoints in edge AZs (platform) 3) sidecar keepalive + connection pooling PR (dev) 4) add cross-AZ NAT and autoscale runbook (infra) 5) increase conntrack targets where needed (infra)
maria: testing show 90% reduction in 5xx after tasks 1+4 executed. leaving monitoring for 1h before closing thread :thumbsup:
jamie: thanks all, adding debrief to incident INC-2026-9042 and scheduling postmortem tomorrow 16:00 UTC
